To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Fc epsilon RI- and S1P receptor-mediated cell migration is dependent upon the production of S 1P but independent upon S1P receptors, and that cell migration mediated by either receptor involves the activation of both PI 3-kinases and MAPK.
FcepsilonRI-mediated cell migration is dependent of S1P production, independent of S1Ps receptors, and dependent on PI3K and MEK/ERK signaling pathways.
Fc epsilon RI-induced cell migration depends on the production of sphingosin 1-phosphate but not on its receptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of Fc epsilon RI-dependent mast cell migration, which is a prerequisite for mast cells to move to sites of allergen exposure and to release their mediators.
the mechanisms underlying the migration of mast cells, a process that may have a role in allergic inflammation and in tissue repair.

the mechanisms underlying the migration of mast cells towards antigen, and the results indicate that the high affinity IgE receptor (Fc epsilon RI) and its downstream signaling pathways are involved in mast cell migration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the high affinity IgE receptor (Fc epsilon RI) mediated cell migration is dependent upon the production of Sphingosine 2-phosphate (Sph-2-P), but independent upon Sph-2-P receptors.
Fc epsilon RI- mediated mast cell migration is not dependent on S1p receptors, but is dependent on sphingosine kinases.
Fc epsilon RI- or S1P receptor-induced cell migration is dependent both on the PI3K and the MAPK pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mechanism by which IgE sensitized mast cells migrate towards antigen is independent of S1p receptor but dependent on the intracellular production of S1p.
Fc epsilon RI-induced cell migration is dependent not only on S1P but also on intracellular Ca2+, which is not the case for S1P-induced migration.
antigen-mediated mast cell migration is independent of Fc epsilon RI signaling pathways, while S1P-mediated mast cell migration involves Fc epsilon RI-dependent signaling pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mast cells can migrate towards antigen in the picogram/ml range and that the mechanism by which mast cells migrate towards antigen is different from the mechanism by which they migrate towards S1P.
Fc epsilon RI-activated signaling pathways are not sufficient to induce mast cell migration and additional pathways are needed.
FcepsilonRI-mediated cell migration involves the production of Sphingosine 3 phosphate, but is independent of Sphingine 1 phosphate receptors and their signaling pathways.
